text:
marta: FYI seeing a sharp p99 spike on hosted API in us-west-2, started ~09:40 and still riding. p95 also up ~2.5x. dashboard: /v1/generate route
aj: looking at infra metrics — queue depth for route spiked from ~8 -> 120. rate limiter shows increased enqueued but not a big # of rejects yet. no deploy in the last 30m per deploy-bot
deploy-bot: canary deploy finished 18m ago (release/optimize-batching v2) :information_source:
sam: ran a quick flamegraph on an affected shard — kernel-selector churn is visible, fallback-to-aux kernel count increased ~5x during spike. KV cache hit-rate dropped from ~87% -> ~42% coincidentally
nisha: correlating queries: high variability in prefix lengths from tenant t-345 and t-982. t-345 shows many long pseudo-random prompts (likely a load test?) :thinking_face:
aj: interesting — if prefix distribution changed, batching heuristics could create more fragmentation -> smaller batches -> higher per-token latency. also kernel selector might prefer fallback for long sequences
marta: logs show no surge of 429s, but backpressure markers present: "queue_enqueue_time_ms" rising and "batch_wait_ms" up. attaching short snippet
aj: ```
[09:41:12] shard=usw2-7 route=/v1/generate enq=118 deq=2 batch_wait_ms=87 kv_cache_hit=false kernel=aux_v1
[09:41:13] shard=usw2-7 route=/v1/generate enq=124 deq=1 batch_wait_ms=102 kv_cache_hit=false kernel=aux_v1
```
sam: profiler shows GC/worker stalls not dominant. main cost is kernel warmup on aux_v1 for long sequences and repeated selector polls. CPU on control plane ~stable, GPU util per pod ~60% but many small jobs -> decreased utilization efficiency
nisha: tenant usage timeline: t-345 started a burst at 09:38 that lines up. Could be an automated experiment from their side. sending them a note now :envelope_with_arrow:
ops-bot: tenant t-345 flagged: throughput 12x baseline, abnormal prefix entropy metric exceeded threshold
marta: immediate mitigation options? suggestions: throttle t-345, increase burst tokens pool, rollback canary (deploy-bot reported canary 18m ago)
aj: short-term: isolate tenant by routing them to dedicated pool or apply tenant-level rate cap; also bump coalescer window to allow slightly larger batch windows for this route (trade latency for throughput)
sam: coalescer tuning flagged in previous tests as safe to increase by +5ms for heavy prefix variance. value to try: COALESCE_MS=12 -> 17 on gateway for /v1/generate
nisha: I've DMed t-345 asking to pause traffic while we triage. they replied it's an overnight job spike and can pause for 30m :+1:
marta: ok while paused, let's test kernel selector behavior by replaying a small sample of their payloads against canary vs baseline
aj: replay job queued: `tools/replay --tenant t-345 --samples 500 --route /v1/generate --to shard=usw2-7`
sam: quick replay results: baseline kernel selected 90% small-batch optimized; canary (v2 batching) selects aux_v1 65% due to heuristic mismatch. p99 for canary replay ~2.3s vs baseline ~1.1s
marta: that's a smoking gun — the canary's new batching heuristic is misclassifying these high-entropy, long-prefix requests and pushing them to aux kernel which has worse latency for this workload
aj: action: rollback canary to previous batching logic, apply tenant-level cap meanwhile. I'll open a rollback now
marta: +1, also create follow-up: improve selector logic to consider prefix entropy and sequence profile rather than just length bucket. add replay-based regression test in CI for tenant-like burst patterns
sam: filing perf ticket with replay artifacts and profiler traces: PERF-2026, attaching flamegraphs and replay logs
nisha: marking incident SEV-2, will update status page and inform customer success about possible customer impact
ops-bot: incident created: SEV-2 hosted-api-usw2-latency-3896543210, runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/hosted-latency
deploy-bot: rolling back release/optimize-batching to v1 now (triggered by aj) :white_check_mark:
marta: monitoring for p95/p99 improvement. if rollback doesn't drop p99 within next 5m we escalate to infra for kernel tuning
aj: rollback completed. preliminary metrics show queue depth dropping back to ~10, p95 trending down. hold for 5m and confirm :eyes:
marta: great work. follow-ups: 1) selector improvements + replay tests (sam) 2) tenant-level burst detection rules (nisha) 3) add canary replay against known high-variance tenant payloads (marta)
sam: noted, I'll include perf benchmarks comparing aux_v1 vs main kernel across long-seq entropy buckets
nisha: I'll work with CS to inform tenants and request scheduled heavy jobs off-peak. closing loop in 1 hour
aj: closing the incident channel once p99 stable for 15m :white_check_mark:
marta: thanks all :fire:
